title: Don Steward's Blog 'Median': A Source of High-Quality Teaching and Practice Materials hing-and-practice-materials/
author: Tom Francome
summary: Tom Francome pays tribute to the late maths educator Don Steward (1950-2020), whose 'Median' blog became one of the most widely used sources of maths teaching tasks in the world since 2007. Francome, who met Steward as a newly-qualified teacher in 2003 and worked with him for years afterward, describes Steward's signature gift for designing tasks with hidden mathematical depth that felt approachable on the surface -- students could complete them like ordinary exercises while noticing and discussing genuinely rich patterns along the way. The bulk of the post announces and explains a major project: with permission from Steward's family, Francome and colleagues at Loughborough University spent significant time scanning and digitising over 140 ring-binders of Steward's original paper notes -- more than 22,000 pages -- now freely available online alongside the existing blog. Francome closes with worked examples from the notes, including a favourite 'two congruent halves' geometry task, illustrating the kind of material now newly accessible to teachers.
points: Francome's tribute is grounded in direct, decades-long personal history with Steward (first meeting in 2003, later working alongside him on the mathematics PGCE), giving the piece authority beyond generic praise.
The core practical news -- over 22,000 pages of Steward's original paper notes digitised and made freely available -- is a substantial, concrete resource announcement, not just reminiscence.

Francome's description of Steward's design philosophy ('sit with a coffee and play... until something lovely happened') captures a specific creative process behind the tasks, giving teachers a model for their own resource design, not just access to finished products.

The 'two congruent halves' worked example anchors the abstract tribute in one specific, reproducible task, letting readers immediately sample the kind of depth-under-simplicity Francome is describing.
quotes: Don Steward's median blog is an invaluable repository of mathematics teaching resources.
Don Steward (1950-2020) inspired countless teachers and learners in his fruitful career as a mathematics educator and resource designer.
Don’s hugely popular blog, where he’s published his delightful ‘tasks with depth’ since 2007, has been a source of reliably high-quality inspiration with millions of views from across the globe.
Don’s notes on tasks for teaching mathematics were stored in over 140 ring-binders.
It took quite a while to do the scanning – consisting of over 22,000 pages and presented somewhat idiosyncratically.
Anyone wanting to know how to create lovely maths tasks might like to know Don’s secret. He would sit with a coffee and play.
